From Joint-Embedding Prediction to World Models: A Survey

Overview

Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) learn by predicting target representations in latent space rather than reconstructing observations. This survey follows their development from self-supervised representation learning toward methods that predict temporal change, action effects, cross-modal relationships, and structured scenes.

We use two views of the literature. The five families below organize methods by their main prediction task. Representation, prediction, intervention, and control (R/P/I/C) describe the capabilities examined in the reported experiments.

Taxonomy

The five families are organized by the main prediction task of each method. Some methods span more than one family.

FamilyMain prediction task
JEPA-F · Foundational / staticPredict missing representations from context within a static observation.
JEPA-T · TemporalPredict representations across time or toward future states.
JEPA-A · Action-conditionedCondition latent-state prediction on actions and their possible effects.
JEPA-M · MultimodalConnect images, language, audio, or other modalities through latent prediction.
JEPA-SC · Structured / scene-centricPredict representations of points, objects, geometry, and relations.

Capabilities

These four levels summarize what the original studies evaluate. A method's family does not determine its demonstrated capabilities.

LevelEvaluation question
R · RepresentationAre the learned features useful?
P · PredictionCan the model predict states not yet observed?
I · InterventionDoes the prediction respond to changed actions?
C · ControlDoes the system use prediction in a feedback loop?
